reasoning: This product catalog system has three natural divisions: (1) Backend API with database, business logic, search, and recommendations, (2) Admin dashboard for product management with distinct CRUD workflows, and (3) Public-facing storefront with browsing and cart integration. These represent different user interfaces serving different audiences (admin vs customer) with shared backend services, justifying 3 subtasks rather than artificial separation.

subtasks.name: backend_api_and_services
subtasks.description: Build the complete backend system using Python/Flask and PostgreSQL. Outputs: (1) Database schema for products, categories, inventory with migrations, (2) RESTful API endpoints for CRUD operations with authentication/authorization, (3) Search API with filtering by price range, category, and rating using PostgreSQL full-text search or indexing, (4) Recommendation engine analyzing viewing history with collaborative filtering or content-based logic, (5) Image upload handling with storage management (local or cloud like S3), (6) Shopping cart API endpoints for session/user cart management, (7) API documentation, error handling, validation, and logging throughout.

subtasks.name: admin_dashboard
subtasks.description: Build the admin dashboard using React/TypeScript for product management. Outputs: (1) Authentication UI for admin login, (2) Product management interface with create, read, update, delete operations, (3) Category management interface, (4) Inventory tracking and update forms, (5) Image upload UI with preview and management, (6) Dashboard analytics showing product counts, low inventory alerts, (7) Form validation, state management (Redux/Context), and responsive design. Consumes backend APIs from subtask A.

subtasks.name: public_storefront
subtasks.description: Build the public-facing storefront using React/TypeScript for customer browsing and shopping. Outputs: (1) Product listing page with pagination and filter UI (price sliders, category dropdowns, rating filters), (2) Search interface with real-time results, (3) Product detail pages with images, descriptions, ratings, and recommendations section, (4) Shopping cart UI with add/remove/update quantity, cart persistence, (5) Viewing history tracking for recommendations, (6) Responsive design for mobile and desktop, (7) State management and API integration with backend. Consumes backend APIs from subtask A.
